title: An Agent-Based Model of the Interaction Between Inequality, Trust, and Communication in Common Pool Experiments
publisher: JASSS (Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation) 25(4) 3; Janssen, DeCaro, Lee

key_points.claim: The ABM represents a commons dilemma as a spatially explicit renewable resource. Agent trust, shaped by observed harvesting and cheap talk, drives harvesting. The model is based on Ostrom's behavioral theory and humanistic rational choice theory.
key_points.evidence_quote: The commons dilemma is represented as a spatially explicit renewable resource. Agent’s trust in others has an impact on the harvesting of shared resources

key_points.claim: The model was calibrated to lab experiment data. The best fit was a heterogeneous population, mostly conditional cooperators sensitive to inequality.
key_points.evidence_quote: a small share of altruistic and selfish agents and a majority of conditional cooperative agents sensitive to inequality

key_points.claim: The best-fit agent mix was 75% conditional cooperators, 9% unconditional cooperators and 16% selfish. It reproduced five qualitative patterns and generalized to a restricted-visibility environment.
key_points.evidence_quote: 75% of the agents were conditional cooperators... unconditional cooperators (9%) and selfish agents (16%)

key_points.claim: Communication raises trust, which explains better group performance. The model used self-reported trust before and after communication to drive dynamic trust changes.
key_points.evidence_quote: Communication increased trust explaining the better group performance when communication was introduced.

key_points.claim: Inequality, trust and communication must all be in the decision-making to explain the outcomes. Agent heterogeneity is key. The effect of communication on trust in non-conditional agent types is not captured.
key_points.evidence_quote: the heterogeneity of agent types is key to reproducing observed patterns

reliability_notes: Full text was fetched. It is a peer-reviewed JASSS article with an open-code badge. It covers a narrow topic, lab-experiment-calibrated commons cooperation, so it applies mainly to the aspects of an artificial society covering cooperation, trust, norms and resource governance.
